some peoples, devils presented themselves
as divided into two groups: evil devils living in
the underworld, and good gods or spirits, demigods,
sacred gods or ancestral spirits,
taking many different forms. The latter belonged to the good
world in heaven.
Ultimately, all of them are devils, playing with
these people by giving them these myths
and this mythological system. People
worshipped both groups of jinn, out of hope and fear.
They even sought to appease the evil devils so they would not
harm or injure them. The film also says
the Maya were obsessed with death and filled the temple
walls with skulls. The same is said of
the ancient Egyptians: as soon as a pharaoh
came to power, he would immediately
begin building an enormous pyramid, perhaps taking thirty
years, roughly his entire reign, and mobilise all
his people to build a pyramid whose sole
purpose was to contain his burial. As we discussed
previously, this is not believable. It is more likely that
segments.review_notes: Predynastic pyramid/conventional tomb challenge retained as opinion, omitted from factual article without archaeological support.

segments.text: these pyramids were built before
the Egyptian civilisation we know. Even if they were built
in that period, they were probably not intended merely as
royal tombs. In any case, that is not our topic.
But it is not as though the pharaoh's entire obsession
in life was to build himself a tomb
and be mummified out of concern for the afterlife. People
generally, especially kings, think more about this world
than the next. Even when they think
about the afterlife and their fate after death, these
idolaters connect it with the myths devils
give them. They worship them in this world
and believe they will save them in the next. The important point,
however, is that this is not an obsession with death. People
generally think more about this world than the next, especially
if they are idolaters. These are all commands from devils
to secure their worship. The filmmaker also says
they visited this Maya site on the day of
the Mexican Day of the Dead, a festival still
celebrated today that has existed for approximately three thousand
segments.review_notes: Three-thousand-year continuous festival history unverified; preserved as speaker’s claim.

segments.text: years, since Maya times. Another striking point is that
it is still celebrated on the same day as
segments.review_notes: Calendar conflation retained, not silently corrected. Huastec comparative source describes several days and a distinct community.

segments.text: Halloween. We explained in an earlier episode that Halloween
originally belonged to a pagan religion: the Irish
and Scots sought to draw close to spirits
on that day. In the eighth century
CE, however, the pope decided to move
All Saints' Day to that pagan festival,
on 1 November. Thus a pagan and a Christian festival were celebrated
segments.review_notes: November 1 statement retained; exact papal/Samhain chronology unresolved.

segments.text: on the same day, also directed towards the spirits of the dead. Then,
when the Spanish came to occupy Mexico,
they combined these festivals into one day. Even
now, Mexicans celebrate on that same day,
1 November. We also find descendants of
the Maya sometimes keeping their dead ancestors'
segments.review_notes: Community-specific skull practices are unverified in original film; do not generalise to all Maya descendants.

segments.text: skulls. They may retrieve the skulls after
the bodies have decomposed, and uncover
or display them only on that day, during
the celebration, so that their ancestors' spirits may rest.
Throughout the year they prepare
by gathering offerings for the festival,
drying certain foods, specifically
foods their ancestors enjoyed before they
died. They then go to the graves, taking
the skulls and offerings, and present them to
the dead, whose presence they say they feel. Then,
after the celebrations and dances, they eat
the food. They believe that when the spirits
come, they consume the spiritual aspect or spiritual covering
of the food, while the physical food itself
remains. They eat it, but obtain no nourishment:
it supposedly has no nutritional value left, yet it must
segments.review_notes: Loss of nutritional value is a belief reported by presenter, not a finding supported by Muslim 450a.

segments.text: be eaten. This reminds us exactly of the prophetic report
in which a delegation of jinn asked him for provisions. He said:

segments.text: Every bone over which Allah's name has been mentioned is yours; when it reaches
your hands, it will be fully covered with meat. The point here is that
jinn ate before the mission of the Prophet,
peace and blessings be upon him. They would find on the bone
that we ourselves eat from, finding meat even when
we have stripped it bare. In the other dimension
where they live, that bone has
segments.review_notes: Other-dimension mechanism is commentary, not the hadith’s explicit formulation.

segments.text: nutritional value. We find the same idea when someone wishes
to make an offering to devils, even if
he regards them as the spirits of the dead. We find this in
Hinduism and Buddhism to this day. Visitors to those
countries—or even to Buddhist restaurants, such as
Chinese restaurants in the West—will find offerings,
fruit or a plate of the food
served to customers, placed on a small
temple-like shrine at the restaurant's entrance. This
segments.review_notes: First-person restaurant observation retained as testimony, not a general ethnographic survey.

segments.text: I have seen myself. They leave it there all day. Afterwards,
the food may be eaten rather than thrown away, but they believe
the ancestral spirits they worship will come and feed
on its spiritual value. Since
the filmmaker did not visit other Indigenous
peoples of the Americas, limiting himself
to Mexico in Central America, I will add,
segments.review_notes: Mexico/Central America geographic wording retained as speech; not used as a technical regional classification.

segments.text: from my study of these peoples, that they too
held similar beliefs. Many
Indigenous North American peoples believed
that any meteor or meteorite they saw either carried
a heavenly message from gods and spirits,
which they could connect with omens and astrology, or represented
ancestral spirits, which they might greet.
If meteorites fell to Earth and they found
the stones, they regarded them
as messages or gifts from heaven. They also used
the metals in everyday life, considering
these to be sacred medicinal stones,
segments.review_notes: Medicinal/sacred power is an attributed belief, not medical advice; no named North American source supplied.

segments.text: used for healing and possessing spiritual power. Water
collecting in a depression formed by a meteorite
was likewise considered sacred.
Warriors dipped their weapons in it
to draw strength, enabling them to kill
their enemies. The documentary's final example is
in Australia again. They visit an island called
Mer, a very small island with four hundred inhabitants,
segments.review_notes: Mer place identified through independent Meriam study; population figure remains unchecked.

segments.text: all Indigenous. They too believe that meteors
and meteorites carry ancestral spirits. What caught
my attention was an elder from this community
telling them: A member of my family travelled
segments.review_notes: Interrupted انتقل قل smoothed; original elder interview not inspected. All following embedded speech remains a retelling.

segments.text: with the ghosts on this island to heaven,
through a meteorite I saw with my own eyes. He regards
this as an unquestionable fact. He then says: When we see meteorites
or meteors falling towards us, we know that these
ancestors' spirits have returned to us once more,
renewing the cycle of life. He says even more explicitly: We see these
spirits sometimes taking the form of animals,
a bird, a dog, a person, or a shadow on
the walls. These are the same forms jinn-devils take when
appearing to people, or the shadow form in which one appears
segments.review_notes: Apparitions/shadows are interpreted by presenter as jinn; no audiovisual or independent causal verification.

segments.text: in its true shape to some people who
worship them, especially when they make offerings.
In this scene we also see a recreation of a dance
they performed for the devils—that is, for the meteors—when
they lit torches and danced, specifically
segments.review_notes: يقصون repaired to dance (يرقصون) from context.

segments.text: at sunset, the same period when the devil is worshipped
segments.review_notes: Universal sunset-worship claim unverified and omitted from article.

segments.text: among all peoples. During the dance,
they try to spot a meteor in
the sky. When they see one, they consider
it a message that their prayers have indeed been accepted
and have reached heaven.
After presenting these ideas, the film
goes to the Vatican Observatory, an old observatory
that also serves as a scientific museum belonging to the Vatican, with
some old meteorites. The filmmaker
interviews a Christian astronomer, a Jesuit,
segments.review_notes: الجزبيت normalised to Jesuit; filmmaker Q&A identifies Guy Consolmagno.

segments.text: one of those considered scholars affiliated
with the church. The discussion was genuinely beautiful. This scientist,
who is also a priest, spoke about
segments.review_notes: Priest retained as the presenter’s label, but independently identified Consolmagno is a Jesuit lay brother; article corrected.

segments.text: contemplating the stars and how this can bring you closer to
Allah, glorified and exalted. Of course, we know that he
worships Allah while associating Jesus,
peace be upon him, with Him. But faith is present, even where
segments.review_notes: Retains speaker’s theological distinction and positive appraisal of wonder at creation.

segments.text: there is association rather than pure monotheism. Here,
contemplation of Allah's creation is right
and sound. It is what we call for and reflect
upon. Everything he said about understanding that Allah is
the Creator, and that all the astronomical signs we see
increase our faith in Allah, is indeed what
we understand, while stripping meteors and meteorites
of associations involving shirk. The film then discusses
the anticipated dangers of enormous meteorites
colliding with Earth, repeating the catastrophe
which, as we said, according to the theory occurred 66
million years ago when a huge meteorite fell in
Mexico, leading to humanity's extinction, or that of a large portion of it.
It cites, for example, Deep Impact, a dramatic film
made in Hollywood in 1998. We see
segments.review_notes: Film title/year retained; actual film scene not inspected.

segments.text: an enormous tsunami following the fall of a huge meteorite,
with a wave taller even than
New York's skyscrapers. We watch buildings and enormous towers
topple like dominoes. Of course, this is
very imaginative. Even if a meteorite that large fell,
segments.review_notes: Categorical wave-size dismissal unsupported by a checked model; not used as scientific fact in article.

segments.text: the waves would not be so large. The filmmaker then
visits an observatory in Hawaii, one of the largest astronomical
segments.review_notes: هوائي interpreted as Hawaii from context, not aerial; observatory and speaker unconfirmed.

segments.text: observatories in the world. The scientist
watching for meteorites there says there is a very small
chance of an enormous comet falling to Earth. We are talking about
a comet, not just a meteorite. But, he says, sooner or
later a very large comet or meteorite will strike
Earth, though not as once imagined or in the form
Hollywood has presented. The best-known example
of an enormous explosion in modern times is the huge meteorite
thought to have struck Siberia,
Russia, in uninhabited forests. This occurred in
1908. Even now, however, some question this
and suggest it may have been the massive explosion of a flying
saucer that fell there. Two stones were recovered
which apparently were neither meteorites nor
human-made. There is no confirmed study indicating
segments.review_notes: Important qualification: presenter says no confirmed study supports the spacecraft/stones claim.

segments.text: that. My point is that there is still no confirmation
that the event was caused by a huge meteorite striking
segments.review_notes: Retains presenter’s uncertainty; NASA account supports a stony-body airburst, not equal evidence for spacecraft.

segments.text: the area. The question is: could such a thing happen
according to Islam? Does Islam allow for a huge
meteorite to strike Earth and extinguish humanity? What we know
with certainty is that we will not die this way.
segments.review_notes: Speaker’s categorical theological assertion, not a current hazard assessment or reader safety guarantee.

segments.text: The signs of the Hour that we know must occur,
including great conflicts and trials. Afterwards, following Jesus'
descent, peace be upon him, and the end of the Dajjal's trial, disbelief will return
to Earth. The Muslims who followed
Jesus, peace be upon him, will pass away. Humanity's final generation
will be a disbelieving generation. How many will there be?
We do not know. But they will be the final generation,
upon whom the Hour comes. Before that, of course, their souls will be taken.
segments.review_notes: End-time sequence and souls-before-Hour wording need scriptural and audio review; do not silently reconcile with a different hadith.

segments.text: Could they be taken through a huge meteorite causing
extinction? In principle, perhaps, but there is no evidence
for that. What matters to us is that this will not happen
now. All these stages must precede it:
the signs of the Hour, trials, great conflicts, major
disasters, the Dajjal, and devils emerging so that we see them,
segments.review_notes: Visible devils/end-time claim lacks a checked specific source in this episode.

segments.text: and the rest of those terrible calamities. We hope
not to witness them, and that our souls are taken before all these
trials. So we should not preoccupy ourselves now with the idea
of sudden extinction. Thus all
the scientists' research and monitoring for a meteorite of that size
segments.review_notes: Retains dismissal of hazard research as speech; article does not endorse it or advise abandoning research.

segments.text: is not useful. Could a smaller one strike
and cause disasters? Yes. But not the extinction
of humanity or every form of life
that this scenario envisages.
Finally, one observation: why did the filmmaker
present Islam only in the form
mentioned at the beginning, linking it with that legend about
Adam, peace be upon him, then saying the Black Stone
was a meteorite, and leaving it there? Why did they not meet
a Muslim scholar, as they met
a Christian scholar at the Vatican Observatory?
Why did they not listen to the Islamic perspective,
which explains our understanding of meteorites, our view
of meteors, and Islam's outlook on
astronomy generally? What is our understanding of
the end times, and of whether
segments.review_notes: اخذ الزمان contextually repaired to آخر الزمان (end times).

segments.text: a meteorite might strike and cause extinction? Unfortunately,
this is their view of Islam: a mythological one. They do not
even want to give themselves the opportunity
to hear Islam's position, its account of history
and myths, its correction of those myths, and its understanding
of the end times. All of this is refused a hearing. They do not
segments.review_notes: Claim about filmmakers’ intentions retained as opinion; full film and response uninspected.

segments.text: even want to ask and learn what we say.
I therefore hope our young people will not be influenced by this
publicity or propaganda, and that we will not be overcome
by a sense of inferiority before Western science,
retreating and becoming embarrassed by accounts of
meteors striking devils. As we discussed in earlier
episodes, the West itself, its scientific and academic
community, and members of Congress themselves have now begun
investigating alien sightings and the
possibility of beings in other dimensions, not
merely on other planets: beings here on Earth
whom we do not see. These beings are the jinn. Thank you
segments.review_notes: UFO/dimensional beings equated with jinn by presenter; not established by official investigations.

segments.text: for listening. Until another episode,
peace be upon you, and Allah's mercy. [Unclear closing fragment]
